decision: The supported passport route owner is Rust only. A Rust-to-Python-to-Rust rollback rehearsal and compatibility with old signing modes are not retirement requirements.
scope: Retire Python passport routes and adapters after Rust parity and protected disposable acceptance, then deploy one aggregate Rust-only beta release and soak it; production is unchanged during this wave.

parity_reference.standard: Preserve the public application lifecycle, tenant authorization, state and error behavior, data groups, bureau submission and polling, and signed callback effects; documented Rust improvements may extend that behavior without losing supported features.
parity_reference.signing: Managed ICAO_EMRTD issuer profile with active organization-bound DSC and CSCA; the signing key remains in KMS.
parity_reference.evidence: Maintainer-reviewed Rust unit, HTTP, database, and contract tests plus a packaged release gate. The optional reusable integration/compliance fixture is not required for retirement.

remove: Rust-to-Python-to-Rust live owner transition and rollback_accepted receipt
rollback probe in supported-consumer and beta acceptance collectors
legacy Python OCI image pin and attestation in the protected disposable plan

disposable Python issuance service, Python owner phase overlay, and Python-specific artifact-key and bureau credential mounts/wiring; retain the shared simulator token and KMS callback credentials used by Rust
retain: cutover drain of Python jobs, artifacts, and active passport Flows
fixed Rust Gateway and Flow ownership and exact native route targets
protected disposable project identity, bounded teardown, and production isolation
Marty simulator submission, batch, and signed callback evidence

pre_deletion_gates.tests: Frozen route/provider parity, KMS issuer profile and certificate verification, tenant isolation, persistence, signed callback, and packaged Rust image tests pass and have no unresolved maintainer review findings.
pre_deletion_gates.protected_disposable: Accept one source-bound KMS Rust passport run with six owned service images, all nine routes, tenant isolation, managed CSCA/DSC and SOD signing, a two-job Marty simulator batch, signed callbacks, and no physical booklet claim.
pre_deletion_gates.continuity: Exercise Rust service restart and resume an existing KMS-backed job in the protected disposable runtime; prove exact owner identity before and after without a Python phase.
pre_deletion_gates.drain: Stop Python passport writers and prove the cutover-drain contract. Preserve or resolve every existing job; do not discard an in-flight job or an unreadable legacy artifact.
pre_deletion_gates.deletion: Delete superseded Python passport code and runtime wiring immediately after these gates pass, before the aggregate beta deployment.

later_optional_fixture: The base, selfhost, and Kubernetes live consumer suite is optional follow-up #944; unit and contract tests preserve those routing models in this wave.

first_cutover.legacy_jobs: A failed drain or other pre-deletion gate prevents selecting the Rust owner.
first_cutover.routing: Select Rust Gateway and Flow ownership together for all nine routes; do not expose a mixed owner or a Python signing fallback.
first_cutover.custody: New passport artifacts, managed signing, and callback verification use the governed KMS paths.
first_cutover.failure: A failed preflight blocks cutover. A failed post-deployment beta probe halts new beta passport writes, preserves existing jobs and evidence, and requires a reviewed Rust fix and retest; it does not switch to Python.

beta_acceptance.deployment: One official aggregate beta-only release with signed source and image digests; production deployment, resources, and routing remain unchanged.
beta_acceptance.simulator: The physical_bureau_* probe names mean Marty synthetic bureau route-compatibility evidence; physical personalization and paperwork are not claimed and physical_booklet_verified is not a Python retirement gate.
beta_acceptance.soak: Run and record the aggregate beta acceptance soak after Python passport deletion and the official Rust-only deployment.

retirement.delete: Remove superseded Python passport route, signing, bureau, and associated runtime wiring immediately after the pre-deletion gates pass.
retirement.review: Independent maintainers review code, commits, and PRs; fix findings and repeat review until no actionable regression remains.
retirement.out_of_scope: A live Python fallback phase, old remote or self-signed signing compatibility, production deployment, and the optional future integration/compliance fixture.
